It sounds like you care deeply about your student and want to help her get the support she needs. I'm not a therapist or mental health provider, so I'm not able to contact her family or make recommendations about medication. However, your observations are valuable, and there are steps you can take.

Consider sharing your concerns with the school counselor, psychologist, or administration, as they can follow appropriate protocols to reach out to the family and connect them with qualified professionals. If you have direct contact with her mom, you could also gently share what you've noticed in the classroom and suggest she consult with their pediatrician or a mental health specialist. Only a qualified medical or mental health professional can assess whether medication or other interventions might be appropriate.

Thank you for looking out for your student's wellbeing. Teachers are often the first to notice when a child is struggling, and your attentiveness can make a real difference.
